summary: Koichi Shinohara works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He served as Professor at McMaster University (~1973–2004), coordinator of the Numata Program at the University of Toronto Mississauga (attested 2004), and Senior Lecturer at Yale University (~2004).

Koichi Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo in 2004 under supervisors Akira Saito and Ekyo Ejima, later holding posts there as 助手 (attested 2005) and 特任研究員 (attested 2015).

Koichi Yokoyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his MA at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1970) studying under Akira Hirakawa, also studying under Gyōin Hashimoto in 1970, and was a 助教授 at Rikkyo University (~1976–2006).
Koin Takada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and under Gyōin Hashimoto around 1937, later succeeding Hashimoto in 1967.

Koji Kamioka was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1963) and under Yutaka Ochihara, later teaching as a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969) and 助教授 at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

Koji Takahashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and earned a doctorate from Bukkyo University by 1991. At Bukkyo University, he served as 助教授 (~1969–1999) and 教授 (~1976–1999).

Kojiro Yoshikawa was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and as 理事長 of Toho Gakkai (~1973–1980).

Kojun Fukui was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Waseda University under Sokichi Tsuda, he served as 助教授 (1936) and 教授 (1941–1969) at Waseda, and as 学長 of Taisho University (1928–1968, 1972–1975).
Kojun Saito was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor (教授) at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Koken Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Rissho University (~1950–1960). He held posts at Rissho University as 助教授 (attested 1972), department chair (attested 1982–1985), and Director/Professor (attested 2000).
Kokyo Kawagishi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as professor (教授) at both Eizan Gakuin and International Buddhist University (both attested 1976).
Konchok Drakpa was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Dilgo Khyentse.
Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso and held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Konchok Zangpo was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Konrad Klaus is an Indology and Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen and completed his doctorate at the University of Marburg (~1980–1985) under Michael Hahn. He held Vertretungsprofessor posts at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn (1999–2001).

Kosaku Hamada was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905), later holding posts at the University of Tokyo (~1905–1909) and Kyoto University (~1909–1938).

Kosei Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1985, doctorate 1994) under Akira Hirakawa. He held posts at Waseda, served as 助教授 at Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006), and was a professor at Komazawa University (2006–2021).

Kosei Tada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Taisho University and served as 理事長 of the Society for the Study of Buddhist Culture (attested 2004).

Kosen Imakita was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Daisetsu Jōen, Gisan Zenkai, Togai Fujisawa, and Kyokuso Hirose at Shokoku-ji and Sōgen-ji. He served as abbot at Eikō-ji and Engaku-ji, and as Doctrinal Instructor in the Ministry of Religion.
